generation.prompt: Edit the FIRST image: the only creative change is the four young brassicas growing in the soil inside the bamboo frame. At present they look like the same seedling stamped four times in an exact rectangle. Show four individually grown, healthy young brassicas of the same crop and planting date. They must be visibly different even printed small. Front left the strongest, broadest plant, around six blue-green leaves of unequal lengths spreading low, a long outer leaf reaching left. Front right modest in size, noticeably smaller and narrower than front left, a slight lean to the right and one curled leaf facing the viewer, offset back from its present line by several centimetres. Back left the smallest, just three or four young leaves unevenly upright, lean to left; back right an intermediate rosette, with a fuller diagonal fan of cupped leaves and the youngest leaves folded in. Let their stems meet the soil at slightly different intervals and depths along two practical planting rows; crop leaves subtend different angles, overlap a little within each individual plant, vary in texture and green tone. None of them is simply a rotated or resized copy of another. Realistic size variation, planted with care, all inside the six posts below the rails; maintain hand-planted spacing. Keep the existing scene exactly registered to the first image; plants and the handful of bare soil they displace are the entire edit. In particular preserve the tennis-ball close-up in its present BOTTOM RIGHT corner, the six bamboo uprights and 12-inch-high horizontal frame, John's pose, hands, clothing and face, the central bed boundaries, and the clear grass cross-path. No new graphic panels, labels, rules or lettering. The original camera image is supplied second as a location check only, the last two are John's face references only. Render exactly this landscape crop and proportions. Natural gardening photograph, April daylight.
